(p-28) Surah At-Talaq

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them at their waiting period﴾ – the verse.

Although this is an address to the Prophet ﷺ, it includes his community. Qatadah narrated from Anas, who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ divorced Hafsah, may Allah be pleased with her, and she went to her family. So Allah, exalted is He, revealed to him: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them at their waiting period﴾, and it was said to him: Take her back, for she is devout and fasts often, and she is among your wives in Paradise."

﴿At their waiting period﴾ means: in a state of purity (tuhr) without intercourse, and this is the divorce of the Sunnah (talaq al-sunnah).

Regarding whether the number is taken into account in the divorce of the Sunnah, there are two opinions:

The first: it is taken into account, and it is part of the Sunnah to divorce once in each menstrual cycle (qur'). If he divorces her three times together in one qur', it is a divorce of innovation (talaq al-bid'ah). This is the view of Abu Hanifah and Malik, may Allah have mercy on them both.

The second: it is not taken into account, and the Sunnah concerns the time of divorce, not its number. If he divorces her three times in one qur', it is not an innovation. This was said by al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him. It has been narrated that "the Prophet ﷺ used to recite: ﴿so divorce them at the beginning of their waiting period﴾." If he divorces her while she is menstruating, or in a purity after intercourse, it is an innovation, and it takes effect. A group claimed that it does not take effect, since it contradicts what was permitted. As for divorcing a pregnant woman, one not yet consummated, a young girl, a woman past menopause, or a woman divorced by khul', there is neither Sunnah nor innovation in it.

Then He, exalted, said: ﴿And count the waiting period﴾, meaning for the consummated wife, since a woman not consummated has no waiting period. He may take her back within fewer than three divorces before the waiting period ends; after it ends she becomes like one of the suitors, and she is not lawful to him after three divorces except after another husband.

﴿And fear Allah, your Lord﴾, meaning regarding your divorced wives.

﴿Do not expel them from their houses, nor should they leave﴾, meaning during their waiting period, because they are entitled to residence.

﴿Unless they commit a clear indecency﴾. On this there are four interpretations:
One: the indecency is fornication (zina), and the expulsion is to carry out the prescribed punishment (hadd). This was said by Ibn Umar, al-Hasan, and Mujahid.
Second: it is abusive behavior toward her in-laws (ahmaʾ). This is the view of Abdullah ibn Abbas and al-Shafi'i.
Third: it is every act of disobedience to Allah. This is also narrated from Ibn Abbas.
Fourth: the indecency is their going out, and the sense of the verse is: unless they come with a clear indecency by leaving their houses. This was said by al-Suddi.

﴿And these are the limits of Allah﴾, meaning and these are the limits of Allah. On this there are three aspects:
One: it means the obedience to Allah. This was said by Ibn Abbas.
Second: the Sunnah of Allah and His command. This was said by Ibn Jubayr.
Third: the conditions of Allah. This was said by al-Suddi.

﴿And whoever transgresses the limits of Allah﴾. On this there are two interpretations:
One: whoever is not content with them. This was said by Ibn Abbas.
Second: whoever opposes them. This was said by Ibn Jubayr.

﴿Then he has wronged himself﴾. On this there are two aspects:
One: he has wronged himself by not being content, thereby earning sin.
Second: in divorcing at a time other than purity, which prolongs this waiting period and harms the wife.

﴿You know not; perhaps Allah will bring about after that some new matter﴾, meaning reconciliation (raj'ah), according to the consensus of the exegetes, if he divorced with fewer than three divorces.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 65, verses 2–3:

﴿When they have reached their term﴾ means: they have nearly completed their waiting period (ʿiddah).

﴿Then retain them in kindness﴾ means: by retaining them, (take back) the return (al-rajʿah, resumption of marital life).

Regarding His saying ﴿in kindness﴾ there are two views:

The first: by obeying Allah concerning the testimony. This was said by Muqatil.

The second: that one does not intend to harm her through the return, by prolonging her waiting period.

﴿Or part from them in kindness﴾ means: by not taking her back during the waiting period, so that it ends while she is in her home.

﴿And call to witness two just men from among you﴾ means: for the return during the waiting period. If one takes her back without witnesses, then concerning the validity of the return there are two opinions among the jurists (fuqahaʾ).(p-31)

﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out﴾ On this there are seven sayings:

First: that is, He will deliver him from every distress in this world and the Hereafter. This was said by Ibn ʿAbbas.

Second: that the way out is his knowledge that it comes from Allah, for it is Allah who gives and withholds. This was said by Masruq.

Third: that the way out is that Allah makes him content with what He has provided for him. This was said by ʿAli ibn Salih.

Fourth: a way out from falsehood to truth, and from constraint to ease. This was said by Ibn Jurayj.

Fifth: whoever fears Allah in regard to divorce, there will be for him a way out in the return during the waiting period, and that he may be like one of the suitors after the waiting period. This was said by al-Dahhak.

Sixth: whoever fears Allah by patience at the time of calamity, He will make for him a way out from the Fire to Paradise. This was said by al-Kalbi.

Seventh: "That ʿAwf ibn Malik al-Ashjaʿi had his son ʿAwf captured. He came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and complained to him of that, along with a hardship that had befallen him. He commanded him to say often, 'There is no power and no strength except with Allah.' His son escaped from captivity, mounted a camel of the people, and on his way passed by their herd and drove it off. Then ʿAwf came and stood before his father calling out to him, and the pasture was full of camels. When he saw him, he went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), informed him, and asked him about the camels. He said: 'Do with them what you wish, and what you would do with your own property.' Then this verse was revealed: ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out﴾ up to the end of the verse."

Al-Hasan narrated from ʿImran ibn Husayn, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever devotes himself to Allah, Allah will suffice him in every need and provide for him from where he does not expect; and whoever devotes himself to the world, Allah will leave him to it."

﴿Indeed, Allah will accomplish His purpose﴾ Masruq said: Indeed Allah carries out His command concerning those who rely upon Him and those who do not rely upon Him, except that whoever relies upon Him, He will expiate his misdeeds from him and magnify his reward.

﴿Allah has already set for everything a measure﴾ On this there are three aspects:

First: that is, a time and a term. This was said by Masruq.

Second: a limit and an end. This was said by Qutrub and al-Akhfash.

Third: a single determined measure. If it is among the actions of servants, it is determined by the commands of Allah; and if it is among the actions of Allah, then concerning it there are two aspects:

First: by His will.

Second: that it is determined by the benefit of His servants.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 65, verses 4–5:

﴿And those of your women who have despaired of menstruation, if you are in doubt, their waiting period is three months, and those who have not menstruated [likewise].﴾ Concerning "doubt" (al-riyba) here there are two opinions:

The first: "If you are in doubt" about them regarding the blood that appears from them due to their old age, so you do not know whether it is menstruation (ḥayḍ) or irregular bleeding (istiḥāḍa); then their waiting period is three months. This was said by Mujahid and al-Zuhri.

The second: "If you are in doubt" about the ruling on their waiting period, so you do not know what they should observe as their waiting period; then their waiting period is three months.

ʿUmar ibn Salim narrated from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, who said: "I said: O Messenger of Allah, when the verses in al-Baqara about the waiting period of women were revealed, some people of Madina said: 'There remain among the waiting periods of women a category not mentioned in the Qur'an: the young and the old women whose menstruation has ceased, and women who are pregnant.' So Allah revealed: ﴿And those of your women who have despaired of menstruation, if you are in doubt, their waiting period is three months﴾ ﴿and those who have not menstruated﴾." He means: likewise, their waiting period is three months, for He made for each qur' (menstrual cycle; here, a cleansing period) one month, because it generally comprises menstruation and purity.

﴿And for those who are pregnant, their term is until they give birth to their burden﴾, so the waiting period of the pregnant woman is the delivery of her child, in both divorce and widowhood.

﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him ease in his affair﴾. Regarding this there are two opinions:

The first: whoever fears Allah in the divorce of the Sunna, He will make for him ease in his affair regarding return (al-rajʿa). This was said by al-Dahhak.

The second: whoever fears Allah by avoiding His disobediences, He will make for him ease in his affair by granting him success in obedience. This is the meaning of the statement of Muqatil.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 65, verses 6–7:

﴿Lodge them where you dwell, according to your means.﴾ He means: the wife's lodging is owed by her husband for the duration of her marriage and during her waiting period (iddah) following divorce, whether the divorce was irrevocable (bA'in) or revocable (raj'i).

As for His words ﴿according to your means﴾ (min wujdikum), there are four interpretations:

The first: "from your capacity," said al-A'mash.

The second: "from your effort," said al-Akhfash.

The third: "from your ability," said Qutrub.

The fourth: "from what you find," said al-Farra'. Their meanings are close to one another.

﴿And do not harm them so as to constrain them﴾. On this there are two views:

The first: regarding the dwellings, said Mujahid.

The second: so as to constrain them in maintenance (nafaqah), said Muqatil. According to Mujahid's view, that it refers to constraint in the dwelling, the ruling is general, covering both the state of marriage and every waiting period, because lodging is obligatory for the woman in a waiting period in every divorce, whether or not the husband has the right of return (raj'ah).

Regarding whether it is obligatory during the waiting period following the death of a husband, there are two views. According to Muqatil's view, that it refers to constraint in maintenance, the ruling is specific to the wife and to the woman in a revocable divorce waiting period.

Regarding whether an irrevocably divorced woman is entitled to it, there are two views:

The first: an irrevocably divorced woman has no maintenance during the waiting period. This is the position of Malik and al-Shafi'i, may God have mercy on them both.

The second: she is entitled to maintenance. This is the position of Abu Hanifa, may God have mercy on him.

﴿And if they are pregnant, then spend on them until they give birth﴾. This concerns the maintenance of a divorced pregnant woman, because it is owed to her for the duration of her pregnancy by the consensus of all, whether the divorce was irrevocable or revocable. The scholars differed only over whether the maintenance is owed to her by her own right if the divorce was irrevocable, or because of her pregnancy, on two views.

﴿And if they nurse for you, then give them their wages﴾. This concerns a divorced woman who nurses: she is owed her wage by the divorcing husband for nursing his infant, because the child's maintenance and nursing are obligatory upon its father rather than upon her. She has no wage if she is still under his marriage.

﴿And confer among yourselves in kindness﴾. On this there are two views:

The first: said al-Suddi.

The second: they should agree, meaning the two parents of the child should come to terms between themselves, when separation occurs, in kindness regarding her wage from the father and her nursing of the child.

﴿And if you disagree﴾. On this there are two views:

The first: you become constrained and quarrelsome, said Ibn Qutaybah.

The second: you differ.

﴿Then another woman will nurse for him﴾. Their disagreement is of two kinds:

The first: over the nursing.

The second: over the wage.

If they disagree over the nursing: if she calls to nurse him and the father refuses, she is compelled to do so; and if the father calls her to nurse him and she refuses, then if he accepts the breast of others she is not compelled to nurse him and another woman is hired to nurse him; but if he does not accept the breast of others, she is compelled to nurse him for the equivalent wage.

If they disagree over the wage: if she demands the equivalent wage and the father refuses except as a voluntary gift, the mother has the better claim to the equivalent wage when the father finds no volunteer.

If the father demands the equivalent wage and the mother refuses excessively, the father has the better claim to it; and if the father then becomes unable to pay her wage, she is compelled to nurse her child for it.

﴿God does not burden any soul except according to what He has given it﴾. On this there are three interpretations:

The first: God does not burden the father with the maintenance of the nursing mother except according to his means, said Ibn Jubayr.

The second: God does not burden him to give charity and pay zakat when he has no property that is charitable or zakatable, said Ibn Zayd.

The third: He does not burden him with an obligation except according to what God has given him of ability; this is the meaning of Muqatil's statement.

﴿God will bring ease after hardship﴾. This may bear two meanings:

The first: after narrowness of provision.

The second: after incapacity of ability.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 65, verses 8–11:

﴿Indeed, Allah has sent down to you a reminder﴾ ﴿a Messenger﴾. The "reminder" (al-dhikr) is the Qur'an. Regarding the "Messenger," there are two opinions:

The first: it is Jibril (Gabriel). In that case both are sent down together (munzalayn), as said by al-Kalbi.

The second: it is Muhammad (ﷺ). The sense of the statement would then be: "Allah has sent down to you a reminder and has sent to you a Messenger."

﴿who recites to you the verses of Allah﴾, meaning the Qur'an. Al-Farra' said: it was revealed concerning the believers among the People of the Book.

﴿clarified, that He may bring out those who believe and do righteous deeds from darknesses into light﴾. In this there are three aspects:

The first: from the darkness of ignorance into the light of knowledge.

The second: from the darkness of the abrogated (mansukh) into the light of the abrogating (nasikh) ruling.

The third: from the darkness of falsehood into the light of truth.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 65, verse 12:

﴿Allah is He who created seven heavens﴾. There is no disagreement among them regarding the seven heavens, that they are one heaven above another.

Then He said: ﴿and of the earth, the like of them﴾, meaning seven. Opinions differ regarding them on two views:

The first, which is the view of the majority, is that they are seven earths, layered one above another, and He placed in each earth of His creation whomever He willed. However, one earth carries them and another earth shelters them, and the heaven shelters only the people of the upper earth, the one on which is our world. Accordingly, the call of Islam (da'wah al-Islam) is specific to the people of the upper earth and does not bind those in the other earths, even if among them there are rational beings of distinguishing creation.

Regarding their seeing the heaven and drawing light from it, there are two views:

The first: they see the heaven from every side of their earth and draw light from it. This is the view of those who hold that the earth is flat (mabsutah).

The second view: they do not see the heaven, and Allah created for them a light from which they draw illumination. This is the view of those who hold that the earth is flat (mabsutah).

The second view: it is related by al-Kalbi from Abu Salih from Ibn 'Abbas that they are seven earths spread out (munbasitah), none of them above another, separated from one another by seas, and the heaven shelters all of them. Accordingly, if none of the people of this earth has access to the others, the call of Islam is specific to the people of this earth. If some of them have access to another earth, it is possible that the call of Islam binds them when it is possible to reach them, because the separation by seas, if it is possible to traverse them, does not prevent the obligation of what its ruling is general. And it is also possible that the call of Islam does not bind them, because if it were binding, the text would have come concerning it and the Messenger would have been commanded with it. And Allah knows best the correctness of what He has kept to His own knowledge and the rightness of what is unclear to His creation.

Then the Exalted said: ﴿The command descends among them﴾. In it are two aspects:

The first: it is revelation, as said by Muqatil. In that case His saying ﴿among them﴾ indicates what lies between this upper earth, which is the nearest of them, and the seventh heaven, which is the highest of them.

The second aspect: the intended meaning of "the command" is Allah's decree and His destiny, and this is the view of the majority. In that case the intended meaning of His saying "among them" is the indication of what lies between the lower earth, which is the farthest of them, and the seventh heaven, which is the highest of them.

Then He said ﴿so that you may know that Allah is over all things competent﴾, because whoever is able over this great dominion, He is more able over what lies between them of His creation, and more capable of pardon and retribution, even though all of that is equal within His power and capacity.

﴿And that Allah has encompassed all things in knowledge﴾ made obligatory the acceptance of what He alone knows, just as He made obligatory the acceptance of what He alone has power over. We seek the forgiveness of Allah from delving into what is unclear and what is obscure, and He is sufficient for whoever seeks His help and takes refuge in Him.
